feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 5 (wheel_radius 0.035 m, 12 mm sensors, iteration 2 body and track, 0.6 kg) scored 51.01, the best so far. Progress was 0.155 on the s-bend, 0.11 on the oval and 0.107 on the slalom, with max_error between 0.061 and 0.066. Earlier iterations showed that span (iterations 0 to 2), footprint (iteration 4), body/track (iteration 3) and controller gains (iterations 0, 1, 4) each left max_error almost unchanged, so the remaining lever is speed. Iteration 3 showed that the narrow, short body lowered s-bend progress, so body and track stay fixed. Body width cannot raise the off-track limit above 0.06 within the allowed range, so I do not suggest changing it. Interpret the next race as follows. If progress rises above 0.155 on the s-bend and slalom with max_error at or below 0.069, mass helps: keep 0.5 kg and try a further reduction. If progress rises but max_error goes above 0.069, the robot is drifting faster than it corrects: return mass to 0.6 kg and try a smaller wheel-radius step. If progress and max_error are unchanged, mass is not the limit, so test wheel_track.
requested_changes: If progress rises above 0.155 on the s-bend and slalom with max_error at or below 0.069, keep wheel_radius 0.035 m and reduce mass further from 0.5 to 0.45 kg. Iteration 5 showed speed helps (s-bend progress 0.15 to 0.155 with max_error held), so lower inertia is the next lever at that speed.

If progress rises but max_error goes above 0.069 on any track, return mass to 0.6 kg and keep wheel_radius 0.035 m. Iterations 0 to 5 show max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.069, so a rise above that band means speed or lower inertia is pushing the robot off the tape.

If progress and max_error are unchanged from iteration 5 (s-bend 0.155, slalom 0.107, max_error 0.061 to 0.066), mass is not the limit. Try wheel_track 0.14 m with mass 0.5 kg. Iteration 3 narrowed the track to 0.10 m and lowered s-bend progress, so widening it is the opposite test.
